claims.author: brunoerg
claims.quote: I think the direct handler calls here (the `CallOneOf` over `protocolinfo_cb` … `add_onion_cb`) hide the paths that need the wire. As far as I tested, no input got past PROTOCOLINFO over the wire.
claims.request: record command verbs in FakeTor and answer the oldest unanswered command with a matching reply so fuzz inputs exercise wire paths past PROTOCOLINFO

status_by.quote: Thanks! I've applied the diff and removed the direct handler entirely since it's not needed anymore, because the fuzzer

claims.status_note: author replied that they applied the diff and removed direct handler calls

claims.author: frankomosh
claims.quote: Could we drop `DynSock::Wait()` entirely instead? The base `Sock::Wait()` already handles this without taking ownership of the socket, and `DynSock::WaitMany()` always returns `true`, so the behavior
claims.request: drop DynSock::Wait() entirely and rely on base Sock::Wait()

status_by.quote: Yes, that looks good,  sorry I missed the `ZeroSock`, thanks.

claims.status_note: frankomosh accepted the explanation about ZeroSock

claims.author: frankomosh
claims.quote: FakeTor already knows when it has sent a correct server hash, so it could record the corresponding expected client hash and assert that every `AUTHENTICATE <hash>` matches one of those recorded hashes
claims.request: record expected client hashes in FakeTor and assert that AUTHENTICATE matches when testing SAFECOOKIE authentication

status_by.quote: Nice! I've added the oracle to verify if the bitcoin node is sending the correct server hash, along others

claims.status_note: author replied that they added the oracle to verify the server hash along with other assertions

claims.author: winterrdog
claims.harm: early exit on exception skips manual CreateSock restoration, leaving it pointing to a destroyed FakeTor instance
claims.quote: if anything exits early (an exception, for instance), the restoration is skipped and `CreateSock` is left using `tor` after `tor` is gone
claims.status_note: author pushed an RAII guard to restore CreateSock on all exit paths

claims.author: winterrdog
claims.quote: i think it is safe to leave out the `COOKIE` authentication method. the controller never uses it (it only acts on `NULL`, `SAFECOOKIE` and `HASHEDPASSWORD`) so offering it does not reach any new code
claims.request: leave out the COOKIE authentication method as the controller does not use it

status_by.quote: if you would rather keep it as a regression guard, could we add a short comment explaining that it is intentionally offered to check that it stays ignored ?

claims.status_note: author explained it acts as a regression test; reviewer accepted keeping it with an explanatory comment

claims.author: winterrdog
claims.quote: now that #36637 is merged, the only thing the `-torpassword` oracle is waiting on is this PR itself, and it is a change to this same file. could it go in here after a rebase ?
claims.request: include the -torpassword oracle in this PR now that #36637 is merged

status_by.quote: I agree with you. Since it's already merged I've add it in this PR as you suggested.

claims.status_note: author agreed and added the oracle to this PR
